It featured a prominent white mokorotlo . The blue stood for sky and rain , the white for peace , the green for land , and the red for faith . [ citation needed ] National flag from 1966–1987 [ 5 ] Royal standard from 1966–1987 [ citation needed ] 1987–2006 [ edit ] A new flag, designed by Sergeant Retšelisitsoe Matete, [ 6 ] was adopted on 20 January 1987, following a military coup which ousted the Basotho National Party after 20 years in power. A light brown traditional Basotho shield along with an assegai (lance) and knobkierrie (club) replaced the mokorotlo as the primary emblem. The colour scheme and pattern changed as

shield along with an assegai (lance) and knobkierrie (club) replaced the mokorotlo as the primary emblem. The colour scheme and pattern changed as well, with a triangular white field standing for peace. The bottom diagonal contained a blue strip for rain and a green triangle for prosperity. [ better source needed ] National flag from 1987–2006 Royal standard from 1987–2006 2006–present [ edit ] In 2006, a new flag was chosen from four proposed designs; all of these designs included a brown Basotho hat instead of the shield. This was subsequently changed to a black Basotho hat in order to represent Lesotho as a black nation. The bill changing the flag was approved by the National Assembly on 18 September 2006, with 84 members of parliament voting in favour of it, 18 against it, and two abstaining.
